subject: Brightline trial acceptance & integration runbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Haskins <ari@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Brightline trial acceptance & next steps

Great chat today — thanks Ari. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment on the 14-day trial and what success looks like. Please reply if I missed anything.

Summary from our call:
- Scope: Brightline will run a 14-day trial against customer support triage (incoming tickets) and a search re-ranking workload. We will provide a hosted trial workspace with streaming generation for triage and embeddings for search.
- Success criteria (proposed):
  * Triage: >85% top-1 intent accuracy by day 10 on your evaluation set (we'll wire up your labeled sample).
  * Latency: P95 generation < 400ms for <256 token prompts at expected concurrency (see ramp below).
  * Cost window: average inference cost below $0.003/token for the triage workload using recommended quantized model profile.
  * Integration: SDK-based streaming prototype and one API route for batch embed extraction completed by day 7.
- Ownership: Redwood will provide a technical owner (Marissa) and SE (Jonas) for the trial. Brightline will provide a point of contact (Ari) and sample data + labeling rubric.
- Ramp & timelines:
  * Day 0 (today): trial workspace created, initial API keys issued (scoped).
  * Days 1-3: ingest sample dataset and configure prefix caching; initial litmus tests.
  * Days 4-7: SDK streaming integration + batch embeddings route wired; smoke tests.
  * Days 8-12: close-loop evaluation vs labeled data; iterate prompt set.
  * Day 13-14: final acceptance window and decision call.

Deliverables from Redwood this week:
- RDW trial workspace + scoped API key (done by EOD Tue)
- SDK route matrix (attached) with suggested streaming endpoints and fallback policies
- Success criteria doc (attached) you can share with procurement

Open items for Brightline:
1) Confirm the labeled sample (min 500 rows) and shared drive link.
2) Approve success criteria above or propose edits by Wed EOD.
3) Procurement: will Brightline accept our standard POC T&Cs or need a purchase order? If PO, loop in procurement contact and timeline.

Next steps: I'll provision the workspace today and loop Marissa to schedule a 45-minute technical onboarding call for Wed (API + streaming primer + test harness). Can we do 10:00am PT?

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189
From: Ari Haskins <ari@brightline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightline.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Brightline trial acceptance & next steps

Thanks Ben — this looks great and matches our understanding. A few clarifications: 

- Labeled set: I'll upload ~800 labeled tickets (intent + priority) to the shared Drive by EOD Tue. Link will be to a bucket for Marissa.
- Procurement: We prefer a short PO for trials to satisfy internal compliance. Procurement is CC'd — we'll aim to get a PO in place by next Friday.
- Metrics: the 85% top-1 target for triage is reasonable; we may add a secondary metric for false positive rate on escalation tags (will loop in details).

10:00am PT Wed works for the technical onboarding. Marissa, Jonas — looking forward to meeting you.

—
Ari Haskins
Head of Integrations
Brightline AI
ari@brightline.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Haskins <ari@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightline.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Brightline trial acceptance & next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Ari. A couple of tactical notes before Wed's call: 

1) Workspace & keys: I've provisioned a scoped workspace (Brightline-Trial-7321) and attached the success_criteria PDF and SDK route matrix. Temporary API key will be sent via the console invite for security (do not paste keys into email).

2) SDK & API routes (engineer-facing):
   - Streaming route: POST /v1/streams/generate?model=rdw-small-quant -> supports partial chunking and tool-calling metadata headers.
   - Batch embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings/batch -> accepts CSV/S3 pointer, returns vector ids + metadata mapping.
   - Fallback route: POST /v1/generate?model=rdw-small-cpu-fallback (auto-routed when GPU pool constrained).
   - Recommended headers: X-RDW-Project, X-RDW-Prompt-Profile, X-RDW-TraceId (for tracing).

3) Instrumentation: We'll provide a small test harness (python) that hits the streaming route and collects latency and top-k accuracy vs your labels. Marissa will share the repo link in the onboarding call; it's a 10–15 minute run to produce baseline metrics.

4) Security: Data-in-transit and at-rest will use your KMS if you choose Private deployment later; for the hosted trial we'll use customer-scoped keys and retention policy of 30 days unless you request otherwise. Procurement, let us know if you need a short DPA addendum for the trial.

Open question for Brightline: do you want us to enable prefix/KV caching for the first week? That will reduce cost and improve P95 for repeated query workflows, but may mask cold-start regressions — tradeoff to decide.

See you Wed 10:00am PT — calendar invite sent.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Haskins <ari@brightline.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightline.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Brightline trial acceptance & next steps

Hi all — quick technical checklist ahead of Wed onboarding (I'll run the call):

Action items (Brightline):
- Upload labeled dataset to shared Drive and confirm column mapping (id, ticket_text, intent_label, priority).
- Provide expected concurrency profile (avg and 95th percentile concurrent users) so we can size trial pool.
- Confirm whether prefix caching should be enabled (see Ben's note).

Action items (Redwood):
- Share test-harness repo + runbook (will attach link during the call).
- Seed workspace with a small synthetic dataset to validate routing and trace headers.
- Pre-load an initial prompt set we discussed (triage templates + re-ranking prompts).

Implementation checkpoints & owners:
- Day 1-3: Data ingest + schema check — Owner: Brightline (Ari) / Support: Marissa
- Day 4-7: SDK streaming prototype complete — Owner: Jonas Weber (SE)
- Day 8-12: Evaluation runs + metric reporting — Owner: Ben Carter / Marissa
- Day 13: Final acceptance check and decision call — Owner: Ben Carter / Ari

Risk flags: if procurement PO is delayed beyond Day 5 we'll run the trial under a scoped evaluation agreement (short-term) but it may delay access to extended logs and longer retention. Please keep procurement updated.

Attachments included: BRIGHTLINE_trials_success_criteria_v1.pdf, rdw-sdk-route-matrix.xlsx

I'll post the onboarding recording and the test-harness link right after the call for your engineers.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Technical Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
